sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Give answer in one word: (i) They are the owners of the company. (ii) Preference shares with a fixed date of maturity.
(i) Debentures with no fixed time of redemption are called ______. (ii) The depository receipts issued by a USA-based bank for trading only in American stock markets are known as ______.
Name the method of finance: sale of an existing asset to a company which then leases it back to the seller.
Which source of finance is called 'ownership capital'?
Fill in the blanks: Loans from financial institutions are granted for a maximum period of ______ years, while commercial banks grant loans for ______ years.
State true or false: (i) A partnership firm can issue equity shares. (ii) Interest on debentures is payable even in loss.
Expand: (i) ECB (ii) FCCB.
questions.answer: (i) External Commercial Borrowings. (ii) Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: State any two needs for long-term finance.
questions.answer: To purchase fixed assets and for modernisation or mergers and acquisitions (also R&D).

questions.q: What is meant by retained earnings?
questions.answer: The part of profit not distributed to shareholders but reinvested in the business (ploughing back of profits).

questions.q: State two merits of retained earnings.
questions.answer: It is cheap (no issue cost, no repayment obligation) and brings financial stability.

questions.q: What is trading on equity?
questions.answer: Issue of debentures enabling the company to earn more for equity shareholders by using borrowed funds at a fixed lower cost.

questions.q: Explain sale and lease back.
questions.answer: The company sells an existing asset to a leasing company and takes it back on lease, releasing long-term funds.

questions.q: What are Global Depository Receipts?
questions.answer: Dollar-denominated receipts issued by an international bank against shares of a company and sold on foreign exchanges; holders get dividend but not voting rights.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Distinguish between equity shares and preference shares (any three points).
questions.answer: Dividend: fluctuating for equity, fixed for preference; repayment in winding up: equity last, preference before equity; voting: equity has voting rights, preference normally not; redemption and convertibility apply to preference shares.

questions.q: Distinguish between shares and debentures (any three points).
questions.answer: Shareholders are owners, debenture holders are creditors; dividend varies, interest is fixed; shares need no security while debentures are generally secured; debenture holders have no voting right.

questions.q: Explain any three merits of lease financing.
questions.answer: Lower investment, tax-deductible rental, no dilution of control and risk of obsolescence borne by the lessor.

questions.q: Explain any three merits of public deposits.
questions.answer: Simple and easy, no charge on assets and economical (also flexible).

questions.q: Explain any three types of debentures.
questions.answer: Redeemable and irredeemable; convertible and non-convertible; secured and unsecured; registered and bearer.

questions.q: State any three demerits of equity shares from the company's point of view.
questions.answer: Higher cost and procedural delay, groups may grab control through voting rights and dividend expectations raise cost.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain any five factors affecting the choice of source of funds.
questions.answer: Cost; financial strength; form of organisation and legal status; purpose and time period; risk profile; control; effect on credit-worthiness; flexibility; tax benefits.

questions.q: Explain the merits and demerits of retained earnings.
questions.answer: Merits: cheap, financial stability and benefits to shareholders. Demerits: possible only when profits are high, may dissatisfy shareholders and may lead to mismanagement of funds.

questions.q: Explain the foreign sources of long-term finance.
questions.answer: ADRs and GDRs, loans from multinational financial institutions, ECBs, FCCBs and NRI financing.

questions.q: Explain the merits and demerits of debentures.
questions.answer: Merits: secured, assured return, trading on equity, no dilution of control and tax saving. Demerits: fixed obligation, charge on assets and reduced borrowing capacity.
